::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[What does integral of a function equals infinity mean](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1978896/what-does-integral-of-a-function-equals-infinity-mean), asked by [srip](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/346394/srip) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-10-21; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> what does a function $f(x)>=0$ for $x>=0$ satisfying $\int_0^{\infty}f(x)=\infty$ mean
:::

It means
$$\lim_{b\to\infty} \int_0^b f(x)\,dx = \infty$$
